cim: Wall Street reels as AI-linked companies spark massive sell-off in the US
cim_eredeti: Wall Street reels as AI-linked companies spark massive sell-off in the US
szoveg_eredeti:
Wall Street closed sharply lower on Friday, November 20, dragged down by the plunge in anything remotely tied to artificial intelligence in what amounted to a total and unequivocal collapse. The dramatic downturn followed the initial public offering (IPO) – the largest in history – of Anthropic, one of the leaders of the AI revolution.

The S&P 500 dropped by 3.7% on Friday and had fallen more than 10% over the month, meeting the standard definition of a "correction" in market terms. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite plummeted 5.28%, erasing nearly 18% since its all-time high on October 6, a time that now feels distant. After several years of double-digit growth since OpenAI released the first ChatGPT model in 2022, the index turned negative for the year. The Dow Jones, where the tech sector carries less weight, lost 1.93% (−8.2% over the month). The US stock market ended one of its worst weeks since March 2020, when the Covid-19 pandemic had triggered a global lockdown.

The numbers are staggering. Since the beginning of the week, companies on the Nasdaq Composite have lost more than $4 trillion in market value – the equivalent of erasing 20 LVMH groups. None of the tech giants – the so-called "Magnificent Seven" – escaped unscathed. Apple fared best, with "only" a 4% drop for the week. Even Anthropic, freshly listed, endured a rough session: Its stock fell 8.5% on Friday, wiping out nearly all the gains from its debut day. Shares opened at $83 on Thursday, soared to $111 by midday, then dropped to $97 at the close. By Friday, the price had slipped to $88.90.
